newsitem.title: USA: Alaska Air spends $10 mln on navigation aids.
newsitem.headline: Alaska Air spends $10 mln on navigation aids.

text.p: Alaska Airlines on Thursday unveiled a $10 million investment in navigation aids to improve landings and takeoffs in difficult terrain.
The new navigation system will be added to Alaska Airlines' fleet of 25 Boeing 737-400s, company chairman John Kelly told reporters.
The Seattle-based carrier will be the first to install both the Global Positioning System and the latest Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System on its aircraft fleet, Kelly said.
The aids will help the airline on flights to airports in mountainous terrain, such as in southeast Alaska.
Two of the carrier's 737-400s already are equipped with the new aids, Kelly said. The 737-400s are the primary aircraft used by the carrier in its Alaska routes.
The airline plans to install the equipment on 14 of its aircraft by mid-February and to complete the rest of the installation by the end of 1997.
